paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is telling me: God is a God of order, and He cares about the details of how His people live. The very first thing in the land is a portion set aside for the LORD (Ezekiel 45:1). Before anybody gets their share, God's share is already there. The people live around His presence, with the sanctuary in the middle and everyone else arranged around it (Ezekiel 45:2-6).

Now look at how much God cares about fairness. He tells the princes, "Enough, O princes of Israel! Cease your violence and oppression, and do what is just and right" (Ezekiel 45:9). Then He gets down to scales and measuring cups: "You must use honest scales, a just ephah, and a just bath" (Ezekiel 45:10). Friend, a LEADER who grabs land and a shopkeeper who rigs a scale are in the same room as far as God is concerned. Whether you're running a country or running a register, what you do with what you have matters to Him.

And then there's the offerings, again and again, for sin, for strays, for the whole people. God says the prince's offerings are "to make atonement for the house of Israel" (Ezekiel 45:17), and that includes anyone who strays "unintentionally or in ignorance" (Ezekiel 45:20). So the heart of it is this, baker: God makes a way for His people to be made right with Him, and He wants them to treat each other rightly too. Keep your ovens warm and your scales honest, because this vision isn't done yet.
